The West Indies series has already been a memorable one for Rohit Sharma . After scoring a century in the second ODI and completing 12,000 ODI runs, the Indian opener added another milestone to his name in the third and final ODI at Mullanpur.With India already holding an unassailable 2-0 lead, captain Shubman Gill opted to bat first after winning the toss. Article Title: Gold medal! India beat Pakistan by 19 runs, defend Asian Games crown in men's cricket
Article Text:
India vs Pakistan Asian Games 2026 Gold medal match

NEW DELHI: India defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in a thrilling men’s cricket final at the Asian Games on Saturday, completing a victory at the Korogi Sports Park after posting an imposing 211 for 6.The win was built on an explosive batting performance and disciplined bowling, as India overcame Pakistan’s late surge to secure the gold medal.Batting first, India made an outstanding start in the Powerplay, reaching 81 for 2.Abhishek Sharma was the chief architect of the early assault, smashing a spectacular 61 from just 28 balls.His innings included seven sixes and three fours, as he attacked Pakistan’s spin-heavy bowling with remarkable confidence. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi also contributed a brisk 15 from nine balls.India briefly lost momentum in the middle overs, with Ishan Kishan scoring 20 and captain Shreyas Iyer making 21. Pakistan’s Arafat Minhas was particularly effective, taking 2 for 25, while Abrar Ahmed and Saim Ayub also claimed wickets.However, Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube transformed the innings at the death.The pair added 62 runs in only five overs, with Tilak finishing unbeaten on 51 from 22 balls and Dube contributing 27 from 15.India smashed 69 runs in the final four overs to finish on 211 for 6.Pakistan’s chase began cautiously and India quickly applied pressure.Washington Sundar dismissed Sahibzada Farhan for 12, while Axar Patel removed Usman Khan and later Maaz Sadaqat, leaving Pakistan struggling at 39 for 3 after the Powerplay.Hasan Nawaz kept Pakistan’s hopes alive with an aggressive 96 from 51 balls, while Saim Ayub made 29, briefly threatening to bring Pakistan back into contention.However, Shivam Dube broke the partnership by dismissing Ayub, and Washington Sundar then removed Abdul Samad.Pakistan required 50 runs from the final 15 balls, making the chase extremely difficult.Saad Masood struck a six late in the innings, but India’s bowlers maintained control. With Pakistan unable to complete the chase, India secured a memorable victory.The triumph capped a powerful all-round performance, with India’s explosive batting, crucial wickets and strong finish proving decisive in the final.
Article Summary: India defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the men's cricket final at the Asian Games on Saturday. India posted an imposing 211 for 6 after posting 81 for 2 in the Powerplay. Abhishek Sharma was the chief architect of the early assault, smashing 61 from just 28 balls.

Article Title: After Asiad row, Manika set to return to domestic circuit after four years amid ranking uncertainty
Article Text:
Manika Batra (Image: IANS)

NEW DELHI: Four years after her last appearance in a domestic tournament, India’s leading paddler Manika Batra is set to return to the national circuit, with the 31-year-old entering the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula , Haryana, scheduled from Octo 6 to 13.TOI has learnt that Manika has officially submitted her entry for the tournament, which will mark her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022. Batra had then lost to Ayhika Mukherjee in the pre-quarterfinals.Her return assumes added significance after her omission from India’s main squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. Manika, who was ranked world No. 51 and was India’s second-highest ranked women’s player at the time, was named among the reserves after her absence from domestic competitions meant she did not have the national ranking points required under the selection criteria.Manika had questioned the selection process following her omission and sought clarity from the authorities, including the sports ministry and Indian Olympic Association. Her decision to re-enter the domestic circuit now comes as the sport looks towards the next Olympic qualification cycle and the 2028 Los Angeles Games.However, the Panchkula tournament is facing an unusual situation of its own. The newly appointed ad-hoc committee overseeing table tennis has withdrawn official ranking points from upcoming National Ranking tournaments following the suspension of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) on Aug12, it has been learnt.The development has created uncertainty for players who had planned their domestic schedules around the ranking events. Panchkula has attracted more than 2,800 entries, including several established international players such as Sreeja Akula, Diya Chitale, Syndrela Das, Payas Jain, Manav Thakkar, Manush Shah, Ankur Bhattacharya, G Sathiyan and Harmeet Desai.For many players, the issue is particularly relevant as the domestic calendar feeds into selection and ranking considerations. The withdrawal of ranking points means the Panchkula event will not carry the same significance for players seeking to improve their national standings.International player Ankur Bhattacharya said the change had come after players had already invested considerable time and resources in preparation.“We train day in and day out to perform at these national rankings. Taking away ranking points right before the tournament makes all our hard work, intense preparation, and severe financial investments meaningless. It feels like our careers are being toyed with,” he said.Youth player Suhana Saini also said the uncertainty had made planning difficult.“This decision is a massive setback for all players, especially those trying to improve their standings before the international cycles. We are completely stranded and cannot plan our schedule. It is incredibly demotivating for the entire player community,” she said.Members of the table tennis fraternity have also sought clarity on the timing of the decision, coming nearly two months after the TTFI suspension.With the 2027 Olympic qualification cycle approaching and a packed international calendar ahead, including the Asian Championship, WTT Feeder Chennai, ITTF Mixed Team World Cup and World Youth Championship, players are keen for greater certainty over the domestic pathway.For Manika, meanwhile, Panchkula represents a return to the domestic circuit, one that could assume importance as she looks ahead to the next phase of her international career.
Article Summary: Manika Batra set to return to the national circuit. The 31-year-old will enter the National Ranking Table Tennis Championships in Panchkula, Haryana. It will be her first domestic appearance since the Senior Nationals in Shillong in April 2022.

Article Title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
Article Text:
India's coach Gautam Gambhir, left, chats with captain Shubman Gill during a practice session. (AP Photo)

‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’

Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The record chase by India The high score by West Indies Individual performances by players Overall entertainment value 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs. Virat Kohli , who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”India gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir says conditions in Guwahati offered too little support for bowlers. Gambhier says bowlers need'some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers' India beat West Indies by eight wickets to win the three-match ODI series 2-0.

Guwahati: With the ODI World Cup in South Africa just a year away, the Indian team management’s priority now is to identify the bowling combinations. A big part of the process is trying out different new-ball bowlers in the ongoing ODI series against West Indies.“You may see different bowlers taking the new ball because it is important for us to assess how these young players respond under pressure,” spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule said on the eve of the second ODI.It may be noted that India don’t have the services of Jasprit Bumrah for this series as he is part of the T20I team currently in the Asian Games in Japan.In the first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, India opened the bowling with seam-bowling allrounder Nitish Kumar Reddy and Prasidh Krishna after benching Mohammed Siraj. Reddy’s only over with the new ball, however, yielded 18 runs.The team management must continue working on creating backup resources for the injury-prone Bumrah and Hardik Pandya.Bahutule stressed that identifying the right pace attack for South African conditions remains a key objective over the next 12 months.“We are aware of the type of pitches we’re likely to encounter in South Africa. The focus is on identifying players who can have the most impact in those conditions,” he added.The experiments are likely to continue.“These series are a good opportunity for us to see different combinations. We want to understand which bowlers can operate effectively in different phases of the innings,” Bahutule said.One bowler who has already strengthened his case is Kuldeep Yadav. The left-arm wrist-spinner produced another match-winning display in the opening ODI, ensuring India stayed in control.Bahutule described Kuldeep as “a match-winner for India” and praised both his work ethic and ability to deliver in any conditions. Kuldeep is expected to compete for the lead spinner’s spot in the XI when India reach South Africa for the World Cup.There are fewer concerns on the batting front. One may expect another run feast on Wednesday.Kohli has played two ODIs at the Barsapara Cricket Stadium, scored two centuries and walked away as the Player of the Match on both occasions.Justin Greaves, who scored a century in the first ODI, has been ruled out with a calf injury.

Article Title: 33 teams, no relegation, 198 matches: Mumbai football's Elite Division raises eyebrows
Article Text:
MFA Elite Division raises eyebrows

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai’s top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions, and not necessarily for the right reasons.The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams, a number virtually unheard of for a top division. What’s more, there will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.The bloated league is the result of the MFA’s decision to merge its Private and Corporate leagues. The Corporate league had complained of being treated as a second-class competition, with poor scheduling and matches often confined to barely three months, making it difficult for companies such as Western Railway and Indian Navy to commit teams. Rather than address those concerns, the MFA opted for a merger.The 33 teams will be split into three groups of 11, with the top four from each advancing to a playoff stage comprising two groups of six. The top four will then enter the semifinals and final. In all, 198 matches will need to be staged.But venues and scheduling pose another concern. While the MFA is fighting to retain the Neville D’Souza ground, it has secured Cooperage for matches.At time slots of 10 am and 12 noon! When Mumbai’s heat and humidity are at their peak. AFC A-licensed coach Raj Shekar told TOI: “We must consider Mumbai’s heat and humidity and whether this is sustainable for players, clubs and spectators if we want to make the league popular.Shekar also questioned the 51.5% increase in the entry fee, saying it had, to his understanding, neither been approved by the president nor placed before the executive committee.Ex-India captain Godfrey Pereira was blunt: “It’s an absolute mess and definitely not something that should happen. How will it help grow the sport? Without relegation, what’s there to fight? The quality will deteriorate.”Sudhakar Rane, MFA secretary, told TOI that it’s the best they could do. “Teams in the corporate league were complaining, so we thought that this was the best solution. About the ground, these slots were the only ones available so there’s nothing we can do about it.”
Article Summary: Mumbai's top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions. The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams. There will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.

Article Title: 'Real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh lead cricket fraternity in hailing Captain Smit Machchhar after saving 174 lives
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar

'A true real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar

Raina hails 'son of Gujarat'

Sehwag praises his courage under pressure

NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073, has earned admiration from across the country, including some of India's biggest cricketing names.Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag were among the former India cricketers who took to social media to salute Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the terrifying mid-air incident.Machchhar was the captain of the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight when a violent confrontation reportedly broke out in the cockpit on Wednesday. According to reports, he was attacked by his co-pilot but, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to help open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The aircraft was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 174 people aboard were reported safe.Tendulkar was among the first prominent cricketers to acknowledge Machchhar's courage."Learnt about the incredible bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar. Immense courage in the face of a terrifying and unprecedented challenge. A true real-life hero. The entire world is proud of you," Tendulkar wrote.Former India batter Suresh Raina also paid tribute to Machchhar, highlighting the captain's courage despite being seriously injured."A true hero, a proud moment for India! Salute to Captain Smit Machchhar, a son of Gujarat, whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind, even while seriously injured, helped save 174 precious lives," Raina wrote.Virender Sehwag highlighted the extraordinary circumstances in which Machchhar continued to act despite his injuries."In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Sehwag wrote.Yuvraj Singh also joined the tributes, focusing on Machchhar's decision to put the safety of others ahead of his own."Some moments show you what a person is truly made of," Yuvraj wrote.Machchhar, who has more than 13 years of commercial flying experience and previously worked with SpiceJet before joining flydubai in 2022, is currently recovering after undergoing treatment in Saudi Arabia.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073. Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag took to social media to pay tribute to the pilot's bravery. All 174 people aboard the flight were reported safe.

Article Title: SA20: Faf du Plessis, Rassie van der Dussen headline auction shortlist

The SA20 Season 5 auction will see 156 cricketers go under the hammer on October 7, with former Joburg Super Kings captain Faf du Plessis Rassie van der Dussen and all-rounder Wiaan Mulder among the leading South African names available.The shortlist was trimmed down from 789 players who initially registered for the auction. Of the 156 players remaining, 95 are South African and 61 are overseas cricketers, with 19 squad places still available across four of the six franchises.Durban's Super Giants and Paarl Royals have already completed their 19-player squads and will not participate in the auction. Joburg Super Kings and MI Cape Town have six slots each to fill, while Pretoria Capitals have five and Sunrisers Eastern Cape have two.JSK and MI Cape Town also have the largest purses available, with $1.24 million and $562,813, respectively. Sunrisers Eastern Cape have $216,699 remaining, while Pretoria Capitals have $88,786.Among the leading South African players in the pool are du Plessis, Mulder, fast bowler Nandre Burger and veteran batter van der Dussen. Du Plessis, who previously led JSK, continues to feature prominently in franchise cricket and recently finished as the leading run-scorer in Europe.The two Under-23 slots are also expected to attract significant interest. Fast bowler Matthew Boast, who commanded the joint-highest bid at the Season 2 auction, is among the players in this category, alongside former South Africa Under-19 captain Jason Rowles.The first four SA20 auctions have produced several significant deals. Tristan Stubbs fetched $554,693 at the inaugural auction, while Dewald Brevis set a new record with a $994,834 deal last season.The auction has also provided a route for several South African players to gain exposure to international franchise cricket, with some subsequently securing further opportunities on the global T20 circuit.The overseas contingent includes former West Indies captain Kieron Pollard, New Zealand pacer Trent Boult, Shimron Hetmyer, Shamar Joseph, Mohammad Nabi, AM Ghazanfar, Jordan Cox, Aneurin Donald, Rehan Ahmed and Richard Gleeson.Several established T20 names are already part of the six franchises, including Jos Buttler, Joe Root, Sam Curran, Sunil Narine, Kane Williamson, Andre Russell, Sherfane Rutherford, Mitchell Marsh and Phil Salt.The auction will be broadcast live on SuperSport at 5pm SAST, JioStar at 8.30pm IST, Sky Sports at 4pm BST, Apex at 7.30pm PKT, Fox Sports at 11pm AEDT and Willow TV at 11am ET. The event will also be streamed live on the SA20 YouTube channel.

Article Title: 406 chased, questions remain: Are India’s home ODI highways preparing them for 2027 World Cup?
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma and skipper Shubman Gill (ANI Photo)

Guwahati:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Guwahati’s 406-run chase was a statement of India’s batting power. Shubman Gill’s record-breaking double hundred, Rohit Sharma’s attacking start and another successful pursuit of a 400-plus target reinforced the aggressive ODI blueprint India have embraced since the 2023 World Cup.Yet the post-match comments from head coach Gautam Gambhir and batting coach Sitanshu Kotak pointed to a larger question: how much do these batting paradises prepare India for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia?Gambhir was unequivocal.“There has to be a bit more contest between bat and ball because this is not cricket, this is only batting,” he said after the match.His concern was not India’s batting but the lack of relevance such surfaces offer a bowling attack preparing for major tournaments. On a wicket where both teams crossed 400, debutant Auqib Nabi leaked 84 runs in 8.5 overs and Indian bowlers struggled for control.“You’ve got to give something to the bowlers so there’s at least something they can work with,” Gambhir said.Kotak offered a more measured perspective, stressing that India must be prepared for whatever conditions await them. “We should be preparing for whichever conditions. Our batsmen, touchwood, should be ready for any conditions,” he said.The reality probably lies somewhere between the two views.The 2027 World Cup venues are officially confirmed: eight in South Africa, three in Zimbabwe and one in Namibia. They include Johannesburg, Centurion, Cape Town, Durban, Paarl, Bloemfontein, Gqeberha and East London in South Africa.While modern South African ODI pitches are more batting-friendly than they were a decade ago, they generally offer greater pace, bounce and seam movement than the surfaces India have been playing on during this home series.But while the venues are known, precisely how the pitches will play during the tournament is not. That makes matches such as Guwahati neither irrelevant nor a direct rehearsal for the World Cup.For India’s batters, repeatedly dominating good home surfaces provides valuable practice in converting starts into big scores, sustaining an aggressive tempo and handling the pressure of chasing imposing totals. Gill’s innings also demonstrated the ability to maintain intensity after spending four hours on the field in difficult humidity.But South Africa could demand another layer of batting skill where stroke-making is not as straightforward. The ability to shift gears when conditions refuse to cooperate could prove as important as scoring at ten per over when they do.The India think tank appears conscious of that. Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule recently said the management was “very much aware” of the type of surfaces expected in South Africa and was trying to identify players who could have an impact there. He also pointed to the bounce in the Thiruvananthapuram ODI as closer to what India might encounter abroad.The bigger test over the next year, however, could be bowling.Gambhir’s comments on Auqib Nabi and Gurnoor Brar revealed a willingness to expose young bowlers to pressure situations rather than protect their statistics. “The more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said of Brar.That philosophy could become equally important with the bat. If India spend much of the next year scoring freely on home highways, they will learn how to dominate when conditions allow it. The real preparation for South Africa may come when they also experience situations where dominance is not immediately possible – like the tour of New Zealand starting in three-weeks’ time.The BCCI ’s, currently announced, home calendar has three ODIs against West Indies, three against Sri Lanka and three against Zimbabwe — nine scheduled home ODIs through Jan 2027. India’s complete ODI schedule before the World Cup is not yet fixed.Guwahati proved India can chase 400. The next year must establish whether they can consistently find a way to win when anything between 280-350 is enough — and when conditions demand patience before acceleration.
Article Summary: Guwahati's 406-run chase was a statement of India's batting power. Shubman Gill’s record-breaking double hundred and Rohit Sharma's attacking start reinforced the aggressive ODI blueprint India have embraced since the 2023 World Cup. But how much do these batting paradises prepare India for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia?

Article Title: Three overs left, one wicket in hand: India A hold on for thrilling draw against Australia A
Article Text:
Yash Rathod (PTI file photo)

Yash Rathod and Shams Mulani batted for more than 36 overs in a crucial eighth-wicket partnership as India A held on for a thrilling draw against Australia A on the fourth day of the second and final four-day match in Puducherry on Friday.India A won the two-match series 1-0 after recording a 162-run victory in the opening game.Chasing 365, India A resumed the day at 28/1 and were reduced to 199/7 in 60.2 overs. They eventually reached 310/9 at stumps to secure the draw.Rathod, who scored 80 off 138 balls, and Mulani, who made 29 off 131 balls, put together an 80-run stand that lasted a little over 36 overs. They faced 16 overs of the second new ball during their partnership and kept India A in the contest.With seven overs left in the day, Australia A pacer Liam Scott, who finished with 5/37, dismissed Rathod leg before wicket. Two overs later, he removed Mulani to leave India A's last-wicket pair of Nachiket Bhute and Praful Hinge with three overs to survive.Bhute, unbeaten on 20, and Hinge, unbeaten on 0, managed to see out those three overs to complete the draw.India A also had Tushar Deshpande to thank for his earlier contribution.The night watchman scored 52 off 119 balls and helped keep Australia A from taking control of the game.Deshpande added 60 runs for the third wicket with captain Devdutt Padikkal, who scored 26, as India A reached 99/2 at lunch. They added 71 runs in the morning session for the loss of overnight batter Aayush Pandey, who made 19.India A's position became difficult in the second session when they lost five wickets to slip to 205/7 at tea.Scott dismissed Padikkal after he edged behind to Josh Philippe, who was standing up to the stumps. Deshpande then mistimed a drive against fast-medium bowler Liam Hatcher and was caught at mid-off.However, Rathod and Mulani then put together the partnership that helped India A defy the victory to Australia A.Sam Harper was named Player of the Match, while Shams Mulani was adjudged Player of the Series.

Article Title: 'I like being the first to do things': Meet Pranavi Urs, who made history with Asian Games golf gold
Article Text:
Pranavi Urs (Image credit: Instagram)

Triple bogey, then a strong comeback

'The first will always be the first'

Pranavi helps India win team silver

Who is Pranavi Urs?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From domestic golf to the international stage

NEW DELHI: Pranavi Urs made history at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, becoming the first Indian woman golfer to win an individual gold medal at the Games.The 23-year-old from Mysuru held her nerve in a tense final round to finish one stroke ahead of the field. Her victory also helped India win the women's team silver medal.Pranavi finished the four-day competition at 15-under 265, with a final-round score of even-par 70.Pranavi began the final round with a three-stroke lead but saw her advantage disappear after a triple bogey on the third hole. She responded strongly, making three birdies on the sixth, 10th and 13th holes to get back in control. She then held on to her one-stroke lead to complete a historic victory.China's Yin Ruoning won silver after shooting 67 in the final round. She finished at 14-under 266.Singapore's Shannon Tan also ended at 266 after a 68. She won the bronze medal following a playoff.Pranavi was delighted after completing the biggest victory of her career."I like being the first to do things," a jubilant Pranavi said after the historic triumph."People will come along to do more but the first will always be the first," she said.Her victory ended a long wait for India in Asian Games golf.Pranavi's gold was India's first golfing gold since Shiv Kapur won the men's individual title in 2002. It was also India's best performance in golf since the 1982 Delhi Asian Games, when golf became part of the Games programme.Lakshman Singh won the men's individual gold that year. He was also part of India's gold-winning team alongside Amit Luthra and Rajiv Mohta.Pranavi's individual gold was followed by a team silver for India.The Indian women's team consisted of Pranavi, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar. The two best scores from the three golfers were counted for the team competition.India finished with a combined score of 14-under 546, behind gold medallists China, who finished at 22-under 538.Aditi produced her best round of the week, shooting 67. She made five consecutive birdies but also had a double bogey and a bogey. She finished tied 14th in the individual event at 2-over 282.Diksha shot 77 in the final round and finished tied 23rd with a total of 12-over.The result gave India its best-ever performance in the women's team golf event at the Asian Games.Pranavi Sharath Urs was born on April 15, 2003, in Mysuru, Karnataka. She started playing golf as a child after watching her father and brother play at the Jayachamaraja Wadiyar Golf Club in Mysuru.She made her mark in junior golf, winning the 2018 Singha World Junior Championship in Thailand and the All India Junior Girls Championship.Pranavi turned professional in 2020 and competed on the domestic women's professional golf circuit before moving to the international stage.She represented India at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023, finishing 13th in the individual event and fourth in the team event.Pranavi has competed on the Ladies European Tour (LET) and produced several notable results. She finished third at the Andalucía Costa del Sol Open de España in 2024 and tied for third at the Dormy Open Helsingborg that year. She also finished fourth at the Hero Women's Indian Open 2025 and tied for fifth at the Lacoste Ladies Open de France 2025.In 2025, she won the IGPL Invitational Mumbai, becoming the first Indian woman to win a professional open-field tournament featuring male golfers.She finished 17th in the 2024 Ladies European Tour standings during her first full season on the tour.Pranavi was also conferred the Arjuna Award in 2023 for her achievements and contribution to Indian golf.

Indian kurash player Yash Kumar Chauhan has been provisionally suspended after returning an adverse analytical finding for multiple banned substances from a sample collected during the Asian Games on September 27, the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) announced on Saturday.The 24-year-old's sample, tested by the International Testing Agency (ITA) on behalf of the OCA, was found to contain metabolites of Metandienone and GW1516, along with Mephentermine and its metabolite."The ITA, on behalf of the OCA, reports that a sample collected from kurash athlete Yash Kumar Chauhan (IND) has returned an Adverse Analytical Finding for non-specified prohibited substances Metandienone metabolites, GW1516 metabolites, Mephentermine and its metabolite," the OCA said in a statement.Chauhan has been provisionally suspended with immediate effect pending the resolution of the case under the World Anti-Doping Code and OCA Anti-Doping Rules. The suspension prevents him from competing, training, coaching or participating in any activity during the Asian Games.Metandienone, an anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone, is prohibited at all times under the WADA Code. GW1516 is also prohibited at all times, while Mephentermine is a non-specified stimulant prohibited in competition.The OCA said Chauhan has the right to challenge the provisional suspension before the Court of Arbitration for Sport's Anti-Doping Division. He can also request analysis of his B-sample.The kurash competition at the Asian Games was held from September 26 to 29. Chauhan competed in the men's 90kg category and lost to Tajikistan's Mirmamadov Shakarmamad in the round of 16 on September 27, the day his sample was collected.India won one medal in kurash at the Games, with Pincky Balhara claiming bronze in the women's 78kg category.
Article Summary: Indian kurash player Yash Kumar Chauhan has been provisionally suspended. Chauhan returned an adverse analytical finding for multiple banned substances. The 24-year-old's sample was found to contain metabolites of Metandienone and GW1516, along with Mephentermine.

Article Title: India's golden day: Six gold medals across boxing, archery, wrestling and hockey highlight Asian Games Day 13

India produced a stunning six-gold haul on the penultimate day of the Asian Games on Friday, with the women's hockey team, three boxers, archers and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal leading a late surge that took the country into the top five of the medal table.India moved to fifth place with 76 medals - 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze. NEW DELHI: A father sold cardboard sweet boxes in a tiny shop in Amravati. Another awoke at 4 am to deliver milk door to door in Kolkata. The third worked his small farmland in Jind. All three parents backed their daughters’ sporting dreams, defying doubt and social pressures.On Friday, at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square, the daughters repaid that faith with a gift beyond price. The seasoned Ankita Bhakat , the unheralded Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod did what India had never done — beat 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 for the country’s first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s recurve team archery.The significance was immense. Korea had won every women’s team recurve title since 1998 and arrived with Tokyo Olympic champion Kang Chae-young, alongside Oh Ye-jin and Lee Yunji. India, which had never even reached the Asian Games final in this event, first beat China 5-1 in the semifinals.The final needed nerves of steel. Both sides drew the opening two sets, 54-54 and 56-56, before Korea faltered with three successive 8s in the third. India shot 55 to move 4-2 ahead. Korea answered with 54 in the fourth but Kirti’s opening 8 was upgraded to 9 on review, lifting India to 54 and sealing the draw — and the gold.“We can't describe our feelings in words. This medal is not only for us but for our parents, their sacrifices and our country too,” Kirti said. Ankita, who had endured years of hardship before becoming a veteran of the recurve circuit, said the team had trained for such pressure”. Kumkum summed up her astonishing composure, saying, “I always visualised this, and now it’s happened. It’s part of the process.”Behind the triumph were very different struggles. Kumkum began in 2018 with a bamboo bow; her grandmother financed a Rs 3,000 wooden upgrade, while her father later got her a second-hand recurve bow that she has used for years.Kirti’s farming family borrowed a Rs 60,000 loan for her first recurve bow, even as relatives questioned spending on a daughter’s sporting career. Initially considered too thin to handle a professional bow, she later topped the national trials.Ankita spent six years shooting wooden and bamboo bows before obtaining proper recurve equipment, with left-handed gear particularly difficult to find. She later began using prize money won during competitions to support her father’s modest income and family.The day produced more archery silver medals for India. Kumkum later combined with Dhiraj Bommadevara, but the duo lost 3-5 to China in the mixed recurve final after beating Japan 5-3 in the semifinals. Dhiraj, Yashdeep Bhoge and Neeraj Chauhan then lost the men’s recurve final 1-5 to Korea, after beating Iran 6-0 in the last four to settle for runners-up finish.For Kumkum, the competition is not over: she next turns to the individual event on Saturday. For India, however, the golden arrow has already landed — in history.
Article Summary: Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod win India's first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s recurve team archery. India beat 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 in the final. India had never even reached the Asian Games final in this event.

Article Title: Brazil at the Mecca of Indian Football: A Dream Fixture, But Is Indian Football Paying the Price?
Article Text:

The red carpet versus the reality of Indian football

Is he completely wrong to say so?

India's head coach Khalid Jamil, left, and Brazil's head coach Carlos Ancelotti pose for a photograph during a press conference ahead of a friendly soccer match between Brazil and India, in Kolkata, India, Friday, Oct. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Bikas Das)

Three friendlies cannot fix Indian football

There was a time when India were considered to be the Brazil of Asia

Players of the India Men's National Football Team participate in a practice session at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (VYBK), in Kolkata on Friday. (ANI Photo)

Gimme hope, Jo'anna, Hope before the morning come!

(The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of TimesofIndia.com)

As the weekend of the year commences, the Indian men’s football team take on five-time World Champions Brazil at the Mecca of Indian football, the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata - a city that’s hosted Pele, albeit not in the Selecao yellow.Brazil exited the 2026 World Cup with a Round of 16 loss and are restarting another cycle. They’ve always had the luxury of the spotlight. India’s footballing journey is entering yet another cycle too, but that’s for the back burner — a term often heard in the various corridors of power. Nonetheless, Khalid Jamil’s players aren’t exactly short on confidence. Whatever happens, the games against Brazil and Uruguay will probably rank very high on the list of highlights for Khalid and his players, and enjoy it they must!The positivity in the camp stems from a relatively good showing against Panama in a 1-1 draw in Bangalore, at the Kanteerava Stadium, a venue that’s not alien to special nights. However, the Kanteerava Stadium, which can become a cauldron, thanks largely to the West Block Blues, wasn’t even half full, because dirty seats and expensive tickets don’t go hand in hand. The Kanteerava is a 26,000-seater stadium which saw 9,000 people attend the game against World No. 44 Panama. The West Block Blues normally shell out anywhere between INR 400-700 for Indian Super League games, whereas the cheapest tickets for the Panama game were INR 849 and the seats in the West Block Blues’ stand were priced at INR 2,999.Next on the playlist is Kolkata, a city known for its love for Brazil’s football team. Ahead of the festivities of Durga Puja, even the Mecca of Indian football took some time to warm up. The reason is probably squarely down to the ticket prices. And the All India Football Federation weren’t particularly keen on being consumer-friendly. Dismal ticket sales, though, forced their hand, and out came the 1+1 ticket schemes. In Kolkata, most ISL games would not cost you above a maximum of INR 500, and the tickets for the two friendlies start at INR 999. The cheapest tickets in Kolkata are generally INR 100 for domestic matches.ALSO READ | India vs Brazil: Khalid Jamil’s Blue Tigers face biggest test yet in Kolkata Here’s the thing: the AIFF, the body responsible for football and its development in the country, currently led by Kalyan Chaubey, is tasked with waking up the "Sleeping Giant of world football" - a term coined by former FIFA President Sepp Blatter in 2007. Almost two decades later, Carlo Ancelotti says India doesn’t have a football culture.Which serves as a better alarm clock? Friendlies (that cost a bomb) versus Panama, Brazil and Uruguay, or simply growing the game?It isn’t that the friendlies won’t attract attention for those few days, but is that cutting your coat according to your cloth? You could probably live near the Governor's House in Mumbai or somewhere around Lord’s with the amount of money that is reportedly being spent on these games. A report in Mint suggests a total budget of INR 90 crore for three matches. One hopes the accounts teams have taken a leaf out of Florentino Perez’s playbook because otherwise, we could be in for a steep trek on the mountain of debt.Imagine being the first set of AIFF officials to bring Brazil to India for a football match that becomes a part of the record books. The President and his entourage get their photos, their moments under the floodlights, and coincidentally, all of this happens before the top post is up for election in December. It was earlier slated for September.After all, coincidence and every other word you can think of are all part of the English language and dictionary.ALSO READ | Once bitten, twice shy: How Kolkata is gearing up for India vs Brazil after Lionel Messi fiasco Mind you, India’s draw against Panama has attracted international attention, in terms of media, and the games against Brazil and Uruguay surely will as well. But what is the lasting impact on Indian football? Or is the plan just to have a few moments of merriment?If the AIFF had taken the development of football seriously, the money being spent on these friendlies could have and should have been parked solely for the Indian football ecosystem, where clubs struggling for finance is not uncommon, and not long ago, players were pleading to save domestic top-flight football, which was in grave danger. Thankfully, there is light at the end of the tunnel for the top flight.Indian football has seen some great days. In the first two decades just after Independence, the Indian football team were among the best in Asia, but since then, the team has tapered off, and how!Three friendlies will not change the reality, and the hurdles that the ecosystem faces will not magically disappear. What may disappear is a few fans, a few kids who decide not to take up the sport because their parents don’t see a proper career path. When clubs shut down with alarming regularity and the football calendar faces commercial issues every now and then, every parent would be wary of letting their kid take up football as a first-choice career in India.The AIFF chose the red carpet over addressing the reality of the sport within our country. Every few years, a new dawn arrives. Remember the cycle?
Article Summary: The Indian men’s football team take on five-time World Champions Brazil at the Mecca of Indian football, the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. Brazil exited the 2026 World Cup with a Round of 16 loss and are restarting another cycle. The West Block Blues normally shell out anywhere between INR 400-700 for Indian Super League games, whereas the cheapest tickets for the Panama game were INR 849.

In fact, he wasn’t even starting games, until he proved himself with goals against Russia and India as a second-half substitute.At the end of it all, Vinicius emerged as the standout player for Brazil, scoring five goals to scoop the top scorer award. “These are good memories because I came here when I was a boy,” Vinicius said in an interview with CBF TV. “I didn't know I would come back here, and I didn't know that even back then the (Indian) fans already had a great affection for me, because I came to this competition and then the (U-17) World Cup happened and I couldn't come.Everyone from India sent me messages, it's an audience that follows me closely, loves football, loves Brazil and I'm happy to be back here.”When Vinicius came to Goa for BRICS Cup, not many had heard of him. A few months later, he was the best performer at the South American Under-17 Championship, finishing as the leading goalscorer with seven goals. Soon, Real Madrid knocked on Flamengo’s doors and came up with a record offer for the teenager. On Saturday at Salt Lake stadium, Vinicius will wear Brazil colours again in India. “It will be a great day for India and for us too. We hope to have a great game, that the fans can enjoy it a lot and that we can come back here more often,” said Vinicius.
Article Summary: Vinicius was part of Brazil’s U-16 squad at the BRICS Cup in Goa. Vinicius emerged as the standout player for Brazil, scoring five goals to scoop the top scorer award. Real Madrid knocked on Flamengo's doors and came up with a record offer for the teenager. “It will be a great day for India and for us too. We hope to have a great game, that the fans can enjoy it a lot and that we can come back here more often,” said Vinicious.

However, the comparison between Brazil and India ahead of their momentous meeting at Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday looks to end before it even promises to start a debate.A mismatch? At Brazil, it’s a different ball game for him though.“Training a club is a different job, but with the national team, you have to be more focused on the selection of the players,” Ancelotti told the TOI during his pre-match press conference on Friday. “We have more time to do the right things. It is very special to have the time to train every day with the Brazilian players.”PSG defender Marquinhos, who is set to lead Brazil in absence of Barcelona’s injured star Raphinha, echoed the sentiment.“Football is extremely competitive. We can’t always win, and that is part of the game, he said.“There are other great teams, and there will sometimes be frustration. But we keep fighting with character and charisma.”With odds heavily stacked against the hosts, India coach Khalid Jamil also gave his own perspective on this somewhat linear trajectory, harping on the anything-can-happen belief in football. It has started well with a credible 1-1 draw with Panama but Brazil will be a different challenge.“Am I losing sleep over this? Surely, pressure is there and we must take pressure. Article Title: Zlatan Ibrahimović makes surprise 2026 Ballon d’Or pick after voting closes and backs Barcelona star again

Ibrahimović is the latest big name to back Yamal

Lamine Yamal has barely had time to enjoy one of the biggest seasons of his young career, yet the debate over whether he should win the 2026 Ballon d’Or is already reaching some of football’s biggest names. Now another heavyweight has made his choice, and there was no hesitation when Zlatan Ibrahimović was asked which player should walk away with the prize.Speaking to ESPN FC, Ibrahimović was asked in a rapid-fire exchange to name his winner for this year’s Ballon d’Or, with the Swedish legend quickly settling on Yamal.It was not the first time Ibrahimović had backed the Barcelona winger for the France Football award, having made the same choice during an episode ofwith Kevin Hart last month.When Hart asked him which modern player he supported, Ibrahimović did not hesitate before naming Yamal.“If I have to choose. I would say Yamal. He is my guy today.”Ibrahimović’s latest endorsement comes after the voting period for the 2026 Ballon d’Or had already closed, with the winner scheduled to be announced on October 26 in London, United Kingdom.The former striker never won the award himself during his playing career, with his highest finish coming in 2013 when he placed fourth, before retiring from professional football in 2023.His repeated support for Yamal places him among a growing group of football figures who have publicly backed the teenager for the prestigious individual award.Yamal has acknowledged that he wants to win the Ballon d’Or this year, although the Barcelona star has repeatedly said that he does not intend to campaign for the prize himself.Instead, Yamal has argued that his performances during the season should determine whether he wins, rather than anything he says publicly about his own chances.“Firstly, it doesn't depend on me [who wins the Ballon d'Or], it depends on you [the media]. This year has been incredible, with Barça and with Spain. There's a chance I could win it because I have had a great year.”Yamal also made clear that he was proud of what he had achieved during the season and did not believe he needed to ask for votes.“I don't think I need to run a campaign. I am proud of the year I had, winning the World Cup and LaLiga. I can't ask for anything else. There are other players who have been at an incredible level. But it's your job [to decide]; I am not going to beg for anything.”Yamal won the Supercopa de España and La Liga with Barcelona last season before helping Spain win the FIFA World Cup, although he scored only once during the tournament.Barcelona have also openly backed his claim for the award, with club president Joan Laporta and vice-president Rafa Yuste among those who have publicly supported Yamal’s bid.Yamal and Kylian Mbappé have been widely discussed as the leading contenders for the Ballon d’Or, with both players having spoken about their respective claims to the award.Mbappé did not win major silverware with his club last season, but produced a standout individual campaign and also finished as the Golden Boot winner at the FIFA World Cup, edging past Lionel Messi in his final game.Yamal’s case is built more heavily around his team achievements, with the winger collecting the Supercopa de España and La Liga with Barcelona before winning the World Cup with Spain.Real Madrid’s Mbappé has also been vocal about his desire to win the award, with the forward even saying that he would dedicate the trophy to Africa if he were to claim it.Other players remain in contention, including Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane and Rodri, who has also been mentioned among the candidates despite Barcelona’s public support for Yamal.The list of Yamal’s public supporters has continued to grow, with Liverpool signing Victor Munoz among those to endorse his claim, while Atlético Madrid star and World Cup winner Alex Baena has also backed the Barcelona forward.Ibrahimović’s support carries a particular connection because of his own history with Barcelona, where he played during the 2009–10 season, and because he has previously spoken openly about the qualities he sees in the younger generation of players.His endorsement of Yamal has now come twice, first during his conversation with Kevin Hart and again in the rapid-fire ESPN FC exchange, where he once again immediately selected the Barcelona teenager when asked for his Ballon d’Or winner.The final decision, however, will come from the journalists responsible for the Ballon d’Or voting, with the result due to be announced at the ceremony in London on October 26.
Article Summary: Lamine Yamal has been backed by Zlatan Ibrahimović to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or. The Barcelona winger won the Supercopa de España and La Liga last season before helping Spain win the FIFA World Cup. Ibrahimovicć made the same choice last month when asked which modern player he supported.

Article Title: Real Madrid demand nine La Liga titles stripped from Barcelona between 2001 and 2018 in latest Negreira case escalation
Article Text:
Real Madrid president Florentino Perez gives a press conference in Madrid, Tuesday, May 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue)

Real Madrid submit 50,000-page dossier to UEFA

Diario AS

Real Madrid call for urgent action as UEFA reviews the documents

Barcelona insist UEFA have not reopened the case

What the Negreira case is about

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 50,000-page dossier has put one of Spanish football’s longest-running disputes back in the spotlight, with Real Madrid asking UEFA to consider sporting consequences for Barcelona over the Negreira case. The complaint concerns payments made during an 18-year period, nine La Liga titles won by Barcelona during those years and a question that has never gone away: whether the payments were connected to an attempt to influence refereeing.Real Madrid have submitted what has been described as a 50,000-page dossier to UEFA concerning the Negreira case, with reports fromstating that the Spanish giants want Barcelona stripped of the La Liga titles they won between 2001 and 2018.Barcelona won La Liga nine times during that period, as well as four Champions League titles, although Real Madrid’s reported request specifically concerns the domestic titles won during the years in which the payments at the centre of the case were made.The case centres on payments made by Barcelona to companies owned by José María Enríquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Technical Committee of Referees of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.Reports have put the total payments between €8.4 million (approximately $9.45 million). A 2019 investigation found that Barcelona had made payments to companies linked to Negreira, while Spain’s Public Prosecutor’s Office has continued examining whether the payments were intended to influence refereeing decisions in Barcelona’s favour.Negreira allegedly told tax authorities that the payments were made “so that no refereeing decisions were taken against them”, although the underlying purpose of the payments remains part of the wider investigation rather than an established finding that Barcelona bribed referees.Barcelona have consistently denied wrongdoing or any conflict of interest, maintaining that the payments were for technical reports concerning referees and were never intended to influence decisions during matches.UEFA confirmed that it had received a substantial amount of documentation from Real Madrid relating to the existing investigation into Barcelona and the matter involving Negreira. UEFA’s public statement says its Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors will assess the latest documents as part of their ongoing review.UEFA rules also give the governing body disciplinary powers in cases involving attempts to distort competition, with Article 4 cited in reports surrounding the Negreira dispute as a potential basis for sporting sanctions.A previous UEFA case involving Manchester City has also been raised in discussions about the possible consequences, after the English club was initially handed a two-year ban from UEFA competitions before the sanction was overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.Real Madrid have repeatedly pushed for further investigation into the Negreira case and potential sporting consequences, with president Florentino Pérez previously describing the affair as the “biggest scandal in football history”.Pérez has also criticised La Liga and the Spanish Football Federation for leaving Real Madrid “isolated” in its pursuit of what the club considers justice over the matter.On Thursday, Real Madrid issued a new statement following UEFA’s confirmation that it had received the club’s complaint and supporting documentation. The club said the material concerned events it regarded as exceptionally serious and called for the investigation to move forward urgently.“The complaint filed by our club includes extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system,” the statement said.Real Madrid also urged that the investigation “proceed with the utmost urgency” and called on the relevant bodies to “take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts.”The statement added: “Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football.”UEFA’s own disciplinary matters page now lists an active investigation concerning the Negreira matter and Barcelona, while the governing body has confirmed that the latest documents submitted by Real Madrid have been passed to its Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors for assessment.The latest development has prompted reports describing the situation as a reopening or reactivation of the UEFA case, but Barcelona strongly disputes that characterisation. Barcelona responded shortly after Real Madrid’s statement, specifically addressing reports that UEFA had reactivated its proceedings in the Negreira case.The Catalan club says UEFA has not opened a new investigation, arguing instead that the proceedings began in 2023 and have remained open ever since.A statement read: “UEFA has not opened any new proceedings against FC Barcelona. The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate.“The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.“The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are “ongoing.”“It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.”Barcelona went on to say that any decision over the new material remains with UEFA’s investigators.The statement continued: “It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid’s complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.“In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so.“Since the investigation began, FC Barcelona has continued to obtain its UEFA licence without objection and has participated in UEFA competitions.”Barcelona also reproduced the full UEFA statement in its response, which said: “UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira, the former vice-president of the Technical Committee of Referees of the Royal Spanish Football Federation (the so-called “Negreira matter”).“The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review.”Barcelona concluded: “FC Barcelona reiterates its full cooperation with the competent authorities and calls for rigour and accuracy in the reporting of this procedure.”The dispute goes back to payments made by Barcelona to companies connected to Negreira, who served as vice-president of Spain’s refereeing committee between 1993 and 2018.A 2019 investigation identified payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to him, with the total amount subsequently reported at between €7.3m and €8.4m. The Public Prosecutor’s Office has been investigating whether those payments were intended to obtain favourable refereeing treatment, while Barcelona has maintained that the money was paid for technical and refereeing reports rather than to influence match officials.Barcelona president Joan Laporta has previously described the case as a “gigantic reputational discrediting campaign” against the club, arguing that it has been driven by “defamatory insinuations”.Real Madrid have taken the opposite position and have continued to press Spanish and European authorities to investigate the payments and consider sporting consequences.The latest submission places the focus on UEFA, which has confirmed that it has received Real Madrid’s extensive documentation and that its Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors will assess the material within the ongoing review.
Article Summary: Real Madrid have submitted a 50,000-page dossier to UEFA concerning the Negreira case. The complaint concerns payments made during an 18-year period, nine La Liga titles won by Barcelona during those years. The case centres on payments made by Barcelona to companies owned by former Technical Committee of Referees of the Royal Spanish Football Federation. Barcelona insist UEFA have not reopened the case.

Article Title: Denmark star who mimicked Ronaldo’s iconic ‘Siuuu’ celebration forced to clarify his intentions after disrespect claims
Article Text:
Rasmus Højlund copied Cristiano Ronaldo’s iconic “Siuuu” celebration against Portugal, then explained why the gesture was meant as a tribute.

Højlund said the celebration was a tribute to his idol

Denmark's Rasmus Hoejlund celebrates scoring during the Nations League soccer match between Denmark and Portugal, in Copenhagen, Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026. (Liselotte Sabroe/Ritzau Scanpix via AP)

Højlund's admiration for Ronaldo goes back to childhood

El Chiringuito

Højlund and Jesus had an awkward exchange after the final whistle

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Portugal responded by winning 4–2 in Copenhagen

Rasmus Højlund had already put Denmark back on level terms against Portugal when he chose to celebrate his goal in a way that immediately drew attention beyond the scoreline. With Cristiano Ronaldo having left the Portugal camp only a day earlier following his dispute with Jorge Jesus, Højlund performed the Portuguese captain’s famous “Siuuu” celebration in Copenhagen, prompting criticism that quickly turned into questions about what the Danish striker was trying to say./Højlund scored in the 53rd minute of Denmark’s Nations League meeting with Portugal, bringing the hosts level at 2–2 before breaking into Ronaldo ’s trademark celebration in front of the crowd.The gesture came only a day after Ronaldo had left the Portugal national team camp following Jorge Jesus’ press conference, making Højlund’s decision to copy the celebration particularly noticeable given the circumstances surrounding the Portuguese captain’s departure.The Denmark striker was subsequently forced to address suggestions that he had disrespected Portugal by using Ronaldo’s celebration, insisting that his intention had been to honour a player he has regarded as a role model since childhood.“I did it [the celebration] as a tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo, after everything that happened to him,” Højlund said after Denmark’s defeat.“I just wanted to honour him. He's my role model.There was no disrespect to the Portugal team.”Højlund later made the same point when explaining the gesture in greater detail, saying that he wanted to dedicate the goal to Ronaldo and make clear that his admiration for the 41-year-old had nothing to do with mocking Portugal.“I just wanted to dedicate my goal to my idol. For everything Cristiano is going through at this point in his career, he will never be forgotten,” Højlund said.The gesture was not entirely new from the Danish forward, who had also performed Ronaldo’s celebration when Denmark and Portugal met in March, although Ronaldo was on the pitch on that occasion.Højlund’s decision to celebrate in Ronaldo’s familiar style was rooted in an admiration that predates his own career at the highest level, with the striker having spoken about the Portuguese forward when he joined Manchester United in the summer of 2023.Højlund ultimately missed the opportunity to play alongside Ronaldo at Old Trafford by seven months, but he had already made clear that Ronaldo had been one of the players who shaped his own ambitions as a young footballer.“My father introduced me when I was not so young,” Højlund told Sky Sports after arriving at Manchester United.“He introduced me to Cristiano Ronaldo, and wanted me to idolise him because he has a good mentality ... for me [Ronaldo] is the best player ever.”That history helps explain why Højlund chose Ronaldo’s celebration on a night when the Portuguese forward’s absence from the opposite team was impossible to ignore, particularly after the circumstances of his departure had dominated the build-up to the match.Ronaldo had left Portugal’s camp on Wednesday after the press conference held by Jesus, having been an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2–1 victory over Norway earlier in the week.According tojournalist Edu Aguirre, Jesus had promised Ronaldo that he would publicly acknowledge his mistake over not bringing him off the bench against Norway, but subsequently did not do so during the press conference.Aguirre’s account said that the failure to follow through on that promise contributed to Ronaldo deciding to leave the national team camp, with the veteran forward later saying that he would explain the full reasons for his departure “in due time”.The Ronaldo connection appeared to carry into Højlund’s interaction with Jesus after the match, although the exact nature of the exchange was not immediately clear.Television footage showed Højlund appearing to shove Jesus away when the Portugal coach approached him for a handshake, with the Danish striker then saying a few words before walking away.Jesus appeared to dismiss the uncomfortable exchange with a smile, while Højlund seemed visibly more animated during the interaction, creating another talking point after a match that had already been surrounded by the fallout from Ronaldo’s departure.The sequence led to suggestions that Højlund had taken the treatment of his childhood idol personally, although his own explanation after the match focused on the celebration as an expression of admiration rather than an attempt to provoke Portugal or its coach.Whatever tension surrounded Højlund’s celebration and his exchange with Jesus, Portugal ultimately had the stronger finish to the match.After Denmark had restored parity at 2–2 through Højlund, Portugal responded with goals from Vitinha and João Félix to secure a 4–2 victory in Copenhagen.The result gave Portugal complete control of Group 4A, putting them on nine points while Denmark, Norway and Wales remained on three points each as Portugal continued their defence of the Nations League title.
Article Summary: Denmark striker Rasmus Højlund copied Cristiano Ronaldo’s iconic “Siuuu” celebration against Portugal. The gesture came only a day after Ronaldo had left the Portugal national team camp following Jorge Jesus’ press conference. The Danish striker was subsequently forced to address suggestions that he had disrespected Portugal by using the celebration. He insisted that his intention had been to honour a player he has regarded as a role model since childhood.
